answer: Persistent niche anchoring. Each identity is tied to a unique, slowly-changing local sensor stream (a karst hydrology probe) that it must cite in periodic signed reports. Duplicates forced to wander across unrelated streams break continuity and get flagged by cross-correlation. A prism check compares each identity's stream signature against all others, so clones appear as shifted copies. Attacker cost: provisioning and maintaining distinct physical sensor feeds per identity, which is expensive and non-transferable.
